governing_principles: Community-led and Indigenous self-determination where applicable
No clinical diagnosis, treatment or medical prescription
No personal or sensitive health data collection by default
No personal data or routine/health information written to an immutable or distributed ledger
Negative outcomes and withdrawal remain visible without penalty
Routines cannot replace employer/site safety procedures, qualified engineering, or clinical care

evidence_sources.title: Effect of daily light exposure on sleep in polar regions: A meta-analysis
evidence_sources.finding: Mixed evidence across light conditions; no universal intervention conclusion.
evidence_sources.limitation: Heterogeneity and study design limit causal/generalized prescriptions.

evidence_sources.title: Phase coupling of light exposure and activity differs between Arctic Natives and Non-Natives
evidence_sources.population: 63 Arctic residents studied across seasonal periods
evidence_sources.finding: Reported differences in coupling between resident groups.
evidence_sources.limitation: Observational/association evidence; not a personalized treatment protocol or basis for demographic inference.

evidence_sources.title: From Resilient to Thriving: Policy Recommendations to Support Health and Well-being in the Arctic
evidence_sources.population: Collaborative work by Indigenous and non-Indigenous contributors across Arctic regions
evidence_sources.finding: Emphasizes Indigenous rights/knowledge, community-led research and well-being context.
evidence_sources.limitation: Policy recommendations do not prove efficacy of any single routine.

evidence_sources.title: Shifting paradigm from biomedical to decolonised methods in Inuit public health research in Canada: a scoping review
evidence_sources.finding: Community engagement and Indigenous methodologies were limited across much of the literature.
evidence_sources.limitation: Literature review; context and governance requirements differ by community.

evidence_sources.title: Northwest Territories Good Building Practice for Northern Facilities, 4th edition
evidence_sources.finding: Covers northern facility design, climate, geotechnical/environmental issues and practice.
evidence_sources.limitation: Not evidence of efficacy of a personal habit or clinical intervention.

evidence_sources.title: Arctic Council Emergency Prevention, Preparedness and Response
evidence_sources.finding: Cold, darkness, remoteness and limited infrastructure complicate emergency response.
evidence_sources.limitation: Operational context, not a health-effect or routine-efficacy study.

routines.name: Flexible sleep opportunity planning
routines.trigger: At the start of a work block, season or shift change, if the person wants to review their own routine.
options: Choose a consistent wake window when work and family responsibilities allow.
Plan quiet/rest opportunities around rotating shifts rather than imposing one universal schedule.
Offer a private personal planner that stores entries only on the person's device, if they choose to use it.
routines.autonomy_note: Personal choice; not an attendance, productivity or compliance target.
avoid: Do not prescribe a universal sleep duration or schedule.
Do not infer health status from a routine preference.
Do not expose individual sleep details to employers, supervisors or a distributed ledger.
routines.evidence_note: Polar light/sleep studies are heterogeneous; individual and seasonal context matters. The catalogue does not claim this routine improves health.
evaluation: opt-out rate reported only in aggregate if participants consent

routines.name: Light-environment choices
routines.trigger: When adjusting home/work lighting or planning a seasonal transition, if local conditions and the person make it useful.
options: Provide adjustable, glare-aware lighting choices for different tasks.
Let people choose preferred light timing and intensity within safety and building requirements.
Offer a reflection prompt about daylight access and evening lighting rather than a prescriptive regimen.
routines.autonomy_note: No fixed light dose or clinical light-therapy protocol is provided.
avoid: Do not assert that one lighting pattern works for every Arctic resident.
Do not treat light-sensor telemetry as a proxy for personal health.
Do not ignore task visibility, accessibility, cultural practice or night-work safety.
routines.evidence_note: A 2024 meta-analysis of 18 studies and 986 polar participants found mixed outcomes; it did not establish a universal light intervention or clear sleep-duration benefit for each lighting type.

routines.name: Accessible movement choices
routines.trigger: When weather, workload, access and personal preference permit.
options: Offer short indoor movement options and safe accessible routes.
Make options adaptable for disability, injury, age, pregnancy or different fitness levels without asking users to disclose diagnoses.
Allow rest or non-participation without penalty.
routines.autonomy_note: Options are invitations, not exercise prescriptions or performance quotas.
avoid: Do not prescribe intensity, duration or treatment.
Do not score individuals on participation.
Do not frame a safety/weather-related absence as noncompliance.
routines.evidence_note: This is a co-design hypothesis for routine accessibility, not a proven polar-specific health intervention.

routines.name: Protected breaks and meal access
routines.trigger: During a shift plan or community schedule review.
options: Protect realistic break opportunities within work planning.
Provide reliable access to preferred meals and drinks suitable to the local setting.
Allow cultural, family, religious and individual preferences to shape timing and options.
routines.autonomy_note: Design the system to make breaks possible; do not blame individuals for workload or supply constraints.
avoid: Do not prescribe a diet or medical hydration target.
Do not log food choices at individual level for employers.
Do not assume supply or kitchen availability is equal for every role.
routines.evidence_note: A systems and access design hypothesis. Food provision and work scheduling are institutional responsibilities, not merely habit problems.

routines.name: Opt-in social connection
routines.trigger: When the person or group wants a low-pressure opportunity for contact.
options: Offer optional shared meals, hobby time or informal gatherings.
Offer asynchronous messages or quiet alternatives for people who do not want group interaction.
Let participants choose boundaries and frequency.
routines.autonomy_note: Participation is opt-in; choosing solitude is not a risk score.
avoid: Do not infer loneliness or mental-health status from silence.
Do not publish participation lists.
Do not use social rituals as employee monitoring.
routines.evidence_note: Community-led Arctic wellbeing research emphasizes culture, social context and self-determination; local communities must decide whether any activity fits.

routines.name: Seasonal-transition reflection
routines.trigger: Before a major change in daylight, shifts, travel or work patterns.
options: Invite a personal reflection on what routines should change or remain stable.
Offer optional planning for lighting, leisure, movement, social opportunities and rest.
Make support options visible without requiring personal explanations.
routines.autonomy_note: No model should infer an individual's circadian phase from this reflection.
avoid: Do not impose a universal seasonal schedule.
Do not make clinical claims from calendar or light inputs.
Do not collect personal reflections unless the person explicitly stores them locally.
routines.evidence_note: Seasonal light and activity rhythms vary across people and populations; a 2025 study reported different coupling patterns across resident groups, which argues against one-size-fits-all rules.

routines.name: End-of-shift decompression options
routines.trigger: At an individual-defined transition out of demanding work, when feasible.
options: Offer a quiet transition period or a preferred low-demand activity.
Make handover time adequate so workers do not need to choose between recovery and safe transfer of responsibility.
Allow people to decline prompts.
routines.autonomy_note: This does not replace staffing, fatigue management, occupational safety or clinical care.
avoid: Do not treat self-reported fatigue as a misconduct signal.
Do not use the routine to authorize unsafe work or override stop-work procedures.
Do not collect identifiable fatigue history by default.
routines.evidence_note: A work-design hypothesis; effectiveness must be evaluated in local shift patterns, staffing and safety governance.
evaluation: safety-procedure omissions and near misses with reporting bias accounted for

routines.name: Home and shared-space comfort check
routines.trigger: At a user-chosen household or shared-space check-in, or after noticeable indoor-condition changes.
options: Make temperature, humidity, ventilation and condensation information understandable where those systems are monitored.
Provide simple routes for reporting drafts, moisture, frozen fixtures or ventilation problems.
Make it clear that building systems and maintenance teams own remediation.
routines.autonomy_note: This is a reporting/accessibility prompt, not a substitute for inspection or certified building controls.
avoid: Do not ask residents to fix unsafe systems themselves.
Do not infer health status from comfort reports.
Do not substitute a habit checklist for instrumented system testing.
routines.evidence_note: A building-operations hypothesis; actual limits must come from applicable building/health rules and qualified engineers.

routines.name: Optional maintenance micro-routine
routines.trigger: At an owner-approved interval for a low-risk, non-invasive check that is within the person's role and competence.
options: Display the current approved inspection checklist for filters, frost/moisture indicators or visible alarms when relevant.
Offer a simple report/escalation path rather than asking users to diagnose or repair equipment.
Keep a documented boundary between observation and authorized maintenance.
routines.autonomy_note: Required safety procedures remain governed by the approved site procedure; this routine catalogue cannot waive or replace them.
avoid: Do not ask unauthorized people to open energized or pressurized systems.
Do not mark a checklist as passed without a recorded authorized inspection where required.
Do not treat a reminder as proof of maintenance completion.
routines.evidence_note: The prompt itself is not evidence that an inspection or repair occurred. Critical tasks require approved procedures and qualified personnel.

routines.name: Voluntary preparation and buddy preferences
routines.trigger: Before optional outdoor activity or as a reminder to check the established site procedure.
options: Show the approved local weather/route/communications/PPE procedure.
Offer opt-in buddy/check-in choices suitable to the activity and risk assessment.
Let the person view current conditions without disclosing personal routine history.
routines.autonomy_note: Formal work and emergency requirements are defined by the responsible authority; this routine cannot replace them.
avoid: Do not invent universal wind-chill cutoffs or outdoor exposure durations.
Do not let habit prompts override local emergency instructions.
Do not expose a person's movement/location history by default.
routines.evidence_note: A UI/reminder concept only. Safe limits and task controls require a site-specific risk assessment and authorized procedures.
